tion characterized by dizziness, vomiting, muscle cramps,
fatigue, and confusion.  Fortunately, under most circum-
stances our bodies are good at telling us when we are nearing
dehydration.  When we feel thirsty, our bodies need water.
However, as we get older, our bodies’ ability to sense dehy-
dration decreases, and older adults often lose the sense of
thirst.  Our need for water increases with exercise; exposure
to hot or even warm, dry, or extremely cold conditions;
pregnancy and breastfeeding; and the use of some
medications.  Nutritionists recommend that we drink 8
or more 8-ounce glasses of water daily.  Many fruits and
vegetables are 80 to 90 percent water.  Therefore, in addition
to the vitamins and minerals they supply, fruits and
vegetables  also contribute to our total water intake.  For
more information on water, see Part II, Encyclopedia of
Foods, page 150.
